newsitem.title: UK: Drought threat hangs over Chile copper - Macquarie.
newsitem.headline: Drought threat hangs over Chile copper - Macquarie.

text.p: Much has been made of the ongoing labour disputes in the copper market, but there is a potentially more serious production problem looming, due to the drought in Chile, brokers Macquarie Equities Ltd said.
"The continuing drought in Chile has been a worry for copper producers in the central and southern parts of the country for the past year," the broker said in its latest weekly report.

Water levels at reservoirs are now at critical levels, and if there is not substantial rainfall in the next two to four weeks there are likely to be cuts in power supplies to several major copper mines in central and southern Chile, Macquarie said.
Rationing has already been introduced for domestic power users in Santiago, so the next step would be restrictions on industrial users, Macquarie said.
Producers in the north, such as Chuquicamata, Mantos Blancos, El Salvador and Escondida are not affected by power shortages.

But there are four big mines around Santiago which could be effected. These are La Candelaria, El Teniente, Andina, and El Soldado, and these account for 695,000 tonnes a year of capacity, or 7.5 percent of Western World mine production.
Additionally, the smelters at El Teniente, Las Vantanas and Disputada, which total some 620,000 tonnes of refined capacity, may also be affected, it added.
